explanation: The pole fires when the model reads computer language rather than natural language: its peak lands on a token of a program's operational vocabulary used as code - a shell/Unix command or its flags (' ssh', ' ls', ' grep', ' make', ' cd', ' -m'), a function/method/constructor name or the punctuation of a call or assignment (' print', '.each', ' new', ' (', '.', ' ='), a preprocessor directive ('#define') or a language tag after a code fence ('``` java', '``` kotlin') - and it is strongest inside code fences, inline backticks, '$' shell prompts and imperative command frames ('run make'). The same words used as ordinary English ('I will make a cake', 'I need to ssh into the server', 'Set the table', 'I find it hard'), narrative or even technical prose, prose parentheses, and plain identifiers or boilerplate inside code ('result', 'value', 'public', 'static', 'int') leave it at zero.
